pages.title: What Came Back
pages.scene: Dawn over ash-house row, frost on returned paper
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: By dawn the whole village knows what broke in the night. Forty strides of cedar stand dark, and the wall's lines are just names now, keeping nobody.
People talk through the plans they suddenly remember making. Jorun unrolls bridge drawings he abandoned twenty years ago. The weaver describes the school she wanted to open.
Without the Rootfire's extra heat, the old mortar begins to crack in the frost. Crews brace the walls and start urgent repairs.

Far below the old kiln, where no root should reach, the lower pipe has gone cold. In Hollow Gate's collection ledger, Ashen Leaf's four-hundred-year flow now reads zero. The entry travels uphill before anyone in ash-house row knows to fear it.

pages.title: The Channel Never Stopped
pages.scene: The east terrace channel, water climbing through frost
pages.speaker: Toma Reed
dialogue: The channel never stopped turning. All night, through everything, it just kept climbing. Ninety mouths, remember. It won't carry the whole village.

We'll need lumber and more hands for the next channel, and a route that won't flood the low fields. Jorun is drawing his bridge again. Sena is nine and furious with ideas. We still need fuel for the houses; the water-screw won't warm them.
Mori brought a spade to the terrace. He wants to help us plant the newly watered ground. I told him to wait for you.

pages.title: What Came Back
pages.scene: Dawn over ash-house row, doors open to the cold
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: By dawn the Register wall is dark and shows only names. The Rootfire has returned the plans, ambitions, and possible futures it stored to the people they were taken from.
There is crying in ash-house row, the good kind and the other kind. The walls groan when the wind leans on them. The granary is being counted twice.
Some families welcome the return of their plans. Others fear they won't survive the cold without the old fire. Both need food and shelter before winter deepens.

Far below the kiln, where no root should reach, a pipe has gone cold. Hollow Gate's collection ledger records the missing warmth. In ash-house row, nobody sees the entry. They are busy counting grain and splitting kindling.

pages.title: A Thin Spring, Freely Chosen
pages.scene: The Reed kitchen, Aren's letter unfolded on the table
pages.speaker: Toma Reed
dialogue: It's going to be a hungry spring. I'm glad the cuts stopped. I'm also scared of what happens when the grain runs low. We need to prepare.
Aren's letter is on my mother's table now. She reads it every morning like it just arrived. That is worth a thin winter. I have to keep deciding that, and I keep deciding yes.
Come to the row tonight. We're setting up shared hearths and working out who needs more wood. We could use your help.

pages.title: The Willing Flame
pages.scene: The Rootfire chamber, one small clean flame, the alcove dusted
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: The Rootfire is small now, and clean. It burns exactly as bright as the futures people bring it, and people have been bringing carved tokens all morning, signed and given gladly, one by one.
The founders' alcove has been dusted. The iron racks stand empty, and Mori has already measured them for ordinary shelves.
Upstairs, the village is learning the new arithmetic. The fire keeps what is given freely, and only that.
Below the floor, the lower seam finds nothing legal left to take and goes cold. Hollow Gate's collection ledger records the missing surplus beside the first willing tally.

pages.title: Bought Honestly Twice
pages.scene: The kiln yard, steam and cold sunlight
pages.speaker: Elder Mori
dialogue: The willing flame may carry a kiln on the worst nights. Aren's channel feeds ninety mouths and warms none of them. I am counting firewood separately now, and every crew wants the same hands before snow.
The alcove is filling again. Slowly, the way it should. Osu of the mill line would recognize this room at last.
Eleven willing tokens to catalogue, three kiln crews arguing over one cart, and a sapling waiting outside because I promised I would be present for one beginning. Bring the spade, child.

pages.title: The Willing Flame
pages.scene: The Rootfire chamber, one small clean flame
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: The Rootfire is small now, and clean. The kiln yard is already cold enough for breath to show.
The willing alcove holds eleven new tokens by nightfall. Eleven, from a village of hundreds. Freely given futures were always poor fuel. They are the only fuel left.
At dusk, the kiln clerk carries the eleven-token count from cold room to cold room. No one signs merely to improve it.
Far below the kiln, the lower draw has run dry and gone cold. Hollow Gate's collection ledger records the loss, but whoever reads that ledger is a colder season's problem.

pages.title: The Right to Be Asked
pages.scene: The kiln stair, Toma turning a blank cedar token over
pages.speaker: Toma Reed
dialogue: Eleven tokens. My mother's is one of them. I stood in that alcove for an hour with a blank piece of cedar, and I couldn't. I keep telling myself somebody has to stay unspent to do the work.
This is what you bought us, friend. The right to be asked. It is heavier than I thought, and I still want it.
People can refuse a token now. We need enough food and fuel that refusing doesn't leave their neighbors cold. Help me work on that.

pages.title: The New Keeper
pages.scene: The Rootfire chamber, the shears at your belt
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: The shears balance perfectly in your hand. That is worse than if they had felt wrong. Upstairs, forty strides of cedar are already learning your grip.
Hoshina's chair is still warm. Her room of stolen futures is yours now, every shelf of it, and the little walking loom goes still when you enter.
The wall has already put out a fresh black flower, and it is not for you.

pages.title: The Chair
pages.scene: The kiln stair door, Toma not coming in
pages.speaker: Toma Reed
dialogue: I'll send someone for Aren's model. You carried it in and made her answer for his work. It needs to come home now.
We watched his machine water fields for ninety mouths without burning one future. Why are the shears still in your hand?
You knew what the shears did to Aren, and you kept them. I can't stay and watch you use them.
Don't ask me to help when the racks fill again. The orders will have your name on them.

pages.title: The New Keeper
pages.scene: The Rootfire chamber, the shears at your belt
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: The shears balance perfectly in your hand. That is worse than if they had felt wrong. Upstairs, forty strides of cedar are already learning your grip.
Hoshina's chair is still warm. Her room of stolen futures is yours now, every shelf of it, and the little walking loom goes still when you enter.
The wall has already put out a fresh black flower, and it is not for you.

pages.title: The Reed Kitchen
pages.scene: The kiln stair door, Toma not coming in
pages.speaker: Toma Reed
dialogue: My mother said Aren's name in that chamber and Hoshina had to remember him whole. You kept the door open long enough for that.
Now my mother keeps asking which part of the night to believe: the person who made room for her, or the new keeper sitting behind the same racks.
I don't have an answer for her. She hasn't said much else since we came down the hill.
The model stays with our family. It is not a token for your new office. Don't send for us when the racks fill again. We both know whose stamp will be on them.

pages.title: The New Keeper
pages.scene: The Rootfire chamber, the shears at your belt
pages.speaker: Narrator
dialogue: The fire settles around you like a coat cut to your measure. It does not celebrate. It has done this before.

In the morning the survey asks, very carefully, how you would like the schedules kept. The clerks have already changed the name on the approvals. The village is quiet, the way a field is quiet under snow.
Somewhere above, the wall puts out a fresh black flower on a stranger's line and marks another future for the shears.

pages.title: The Next Black Flower
pages.scene: The Register hall, Mori beside a new line in the bloom chart
pages.speaker: Elder Mori
dialogue: A black flower opened this morning. I wrote the family's name, what the child builds, and the hour the survey noticed. No blessing. No euphemism.
When the gray coats come, I will bring the family to your chamber before you touch the shears. You will hear what they mean to become while the answer can still inconvenience you.
The family is waiting outside my study now. I told them I would bring them your answer myself.
